quality_concepts.title: Learn 5S
quality_concepts.description:
5S — KEY STEPS FOR INDUSTRIES

1. SORT
   • Identify what is necessary and what is unnecessary.
   • Remove obsolete, damaged, duplicate or unused items.
   • Keep only what is required for the work.
   • Dispose of or control unwanted items through approved procedures.

2. SET IN ORDER
   • Give every required item a clearly defined location.
   • Arrange tools, materials and documents according to frequency and sequence of use.
   • Use labels, markings, storage locations and visual controls.
   • Make required items easy to find, use and return.

3. SHINE
   • Clean the workplace, equipment and work areas regularly.
   • Treat cleaning as an inspection activity, not only housekeeping.
   • Identify leaks, damage, abnormalities and unsafe conditions.
   • Correct or report problems through the appropriate system.

4. STANDARDIZE
   • Establish simple and documented workplace standards.
   • Define responsibilities, cleaning schedules and inspection routines.
   • Use checklists, visual standards and standard work instructions.
   • Ensure employees follow the same agreed process.

5. SUSTAIN
   • Make 5S part of everyday work—not a one-time activity.
   • Conduct periodic inspections and internal 5S audits.
   • Track observations, corrective actions and improvement opportunities.
   • Involve workers and supervisors in continuous improvement.
   • Review standards whenever processes, equipment or risks change.

6. SAFETY & COMPLIANCE
   • Identify workplace hazards and implement appropriate controls.
   • Keep emergency exits, fire equipment, electrical panels and safety equipment accessible.
   • Follow applicable occupational-health-and-safety laws, regulations and organizational procedures.
   • Provide appropriate training, competence and personal protective equipment where required.
   • Maintain records and evidence required by applicable systems and regulations.

7. CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT
   • Do not stop after achieving a clean and organized workplace.
   • Identify recurring problems and eliminate their root causes.
   • Encourage employee suggestions and corrective actions.
   • Measure performance and continuously improve workplace standards.

CORE PRINCIPLE:
“Right item. Right place. Right condition. Right standard. Every day.”

quality_concepts.title: Learn LEAN QC
quality_concepts.description:
LEAN PRINCIPLES — KEY STEPS

1. DEFINE VALUE
   • Understand what the customer actually needs.
   • Identify what creates value from the customer’s perspective.
   • Eliminate activities that do not contribute to that value.

2. MAP THE VALUE STREAM
   • Map the complete process from beginning to end.
   • Identify every step involved in delivering the product or service.
   • Detect waste, delays, bottlenecks and unnecessary movement.
   • Focus improvement efforts on the areas creating the greatest waste.

3. CREATE FLOW
   • Ensure work moves smoothly through the process.
   • Reduce interruptions, waiting time and bottlenecks.
   • Balance processes according to actual demand.
   • Maintain a consistent and efficient workflow.

4. ESTABLISH PULL
   • Produce or deliver based on actual customer demand.
   • Avoid unnecessary production, inventory and resource use.
   • Supply materials and services when they are required.
   • Use demand-driven systems wherever practical.

5. PURSUE PERFECTION
   • Continuously identify and eliminate waste.
   • Encourage employees to suggest improvements.
   • Measure performance and review results regularly.
   • Standardize successful improvements.
   • Treat continuous improvement as an ongoing process.

CORE PRINCIPLE:
“Create maximum customer value with minimum waste through continuous improvement.”

quality_concepts.title: Learn 6 SIGMA
quality_concepts.description:
SIX SIGMA — KEY STEPS

1. DEFINE
   • Clearly define the problem, customer requirements and project objectives.
   • Establish the scope, expected outcomes and measurable goals.
   • Ensure the project addresses a genuine business or process need.

2. MEASURE
   • Establish reliable measures for current process performance.
   • Collect relevant and accurate data.
   • Determine the current baseline and identify performance gaps.
   • Verify that measurement methods are consistent and appropriate.

3. ANALYZE
   • Examine the collected data to understand process performance.
   • Identify patterns, variations and potential causes of problems.
   • Use appropriate analytical methods to determine root causes.
   • Validate important findings with objective evidence.

4. IMPROVE
   • Develop solutions that address verified root causes.
   • Test improvements before full implementation where appropriate.
   • Evaluate the effect of changes using measurable results.
   • Implement effective solutions in a controlled manner.

5. CONTROL
   • Establish controls to maintain the improved process.
   • Standardize successful methods and document requirements.
   • Monitor key performance indicators and process variation.
   • Respond promptly when performance moves outside defined limits.
   • Continue reviewing the process for further improvement.

CORE PRINCIPLE:
“Use data and structured problem-solving to reduce variation, improve performance and deliver consistent value.”

quality_concepts.title: Learn KAIZEN
quality_concepts.description:
KAIZEN — KEY PRINCIPLES

1. IDENTIFY OPPORTUNITIES
   • Observe the workplace and identify areas that can be improved.
   • Focus on problems, inefficiencies, delays and recurring issues.
   • Use facts and observations rather than assumptions.

2. INVOLVE PEOPLE
   • Encourage employees at every level to contribute ideas.
   • Create an environment where improvement suggestions are welcomed.
   • Use the knowledge and experience of people closest to the process.

3. IMPROVE IN SMALL STEPS
   • Prefer practical, incremental improvements where appropriate.
   • Test changes before wider implementation.
   • Avoid unnecessary complexity when a simple improvement can solve the problem.

4. ELIMINATE WASTE
   • Identify unnecessary activities, waiting, movement, defects and resource usage.
   • Reduce activities that do not create value.
   • Improve the use of time, materials, equipment and human effort.

5. STANDARDIZE IMPROVEMENTS
   • Document successful improvements.
   • Update standard work, procedures and visual controls.
   • Ensure the improved method is consistently followed.

6. CHECK THE RESULTS
   • Measure whether the improvement achieved its intended result.
   • Compare performance before and after the change.
   • Use evidence to determine whether further action is required.

7. CONTINUE THE CYCLE
   • Treat improvement as an ongoing activity.
   • Regularly review processes and identify new opportunities.
   • Build continuous improvement into everyday work.

CORE PRINCIPLE:
“Small, consistent improvements—made by everyone, every day—create lasting progress.”

quality_concepts.title: NEW TOOLS
quality_concepts.description:
NEW TOOLS — KEY AREAS

1. DATA ANALYSIS
   • Convert process data into meaningful information.
   • Identify trends, patterns and performance gaps.
   • Use evidence to support improvement decisions.

2. PROCESS MAPPING
   • Visualize the complete workflow from start to finish.
   • Identify unnecessary steps, delays and bottlenecks.
   • Simplify processes wherever practical.

3. VISUAL MANAGEMENT
   • Make important information easy to see and understand.
   • Use charts, boards, indicators, labels and visual controls.
   • Monitor performance and abnormalities at a glance.

4. PROBLEM SOLVING
   • Define problems clearly before taking corrective action.
   • Identify and verify the underlying causes.
   • Implement practical solutions and evaluate their results.

5. TEAM COLLABORATION
   • Involve people who understand the process.
   • Encourage ideas, observations and improvement suggestions.
   • Build shared ownership of improvement activities.

6. ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS
   • Look beyond symptoms to identify the actual cause.
   • Use structured methods and objective evidence.
   • Prevent recurrence by addressing verified root causes.

CORE PRINCIPLE:
“Use the right tools, involve the right people, and turn problems into measurable improvements.”

quality_concepts.title: Learn TQM
quality_concepts.description:
TQM — TOTAL QUALITY MANAGEMENT

1. FOCUS ON THE CUSTOMER
   • Understand customer needs, expectations and requirements.
   • Deliver products and services that consistently meet those requirements.
   • Use customer feedback to identify opportunities for improvement.

2. CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT
   • Regularly identify opportunities to improve processes and performance.
   • Reduce waste, variation, defects and unnecessary activities.
   • Encourage small, consistent improvements across the organization.

3. QUALITY IMPROVEMENT
   • Build quality into every process rather than relying only on final inspection.
   • Prevent defects and address problems at their source.
   • Maintain consistent standards across products, services and operations.

4. ACCURATE EVALUATION
   • Measure performance using reliable and relevant data.
   • Review results against defined objectives and standards.
   • Use evidence to identify gaps and guide improvement actions.

5. INVOLVE ALL EMPLOYEES
   • Encourage employees at every level to participate in quality improvement.
   • Value ideas, knowledge and experience from people closest to the work.
   • Build shared responsibility for quality and organizational performance.

CORE PRINCIPLE:
“Quality is everyone’s responsibility—built into every process, measured with evidence, and improved continuously.”

quality_concepts.title: Learn QC
quality_concepts.description:
LEARN QC — QUALITY CONTROL FUNDAMENTALS

1. UNDERSTAND QUALITY
   • Know the required specifications, standards and acceptance criteria.
   • Understand what “conforming” and “non-conforming” mean.
   • Focus on preventing defects, not only detecting them.

2. INSPECT & MEASURE
   • Check materials, components and products against defined requirements.
   • Use appropriate and calibrated measuring instruments.
   • Record measurements accurately and consistently.

3. IDENTIFY DEFECTS
   • Detect deviations from specifications as early as possible.
   • Classify defects according to their type, severity and impact.
   • Prevent non-conforming products from moving to the next stage.

4. ANALYZE THE CAUSE
   • Investigate why the defect occurred.
   • Use data and structured problem-solving methods.
   • Distinguish the root cause from the visible symptom.

5. TAKE CORRECTIVE ACTION
   • Correct identified problems through controlled actions.
   • Address the cause to prevent recurrence.
   • Verify whether the corrective action is effective.

6. STANDARDIZE & DOCUMENT
   • Maintain inspection procedures, specifications and records.
   • Follow approved work instructions and quality standards.
   • Keep traceable evidence of inspections and corrective actions.

7. PREVENT RECURRENCE
   • Monitor process performance continuously.
   • Identify recurring defects and improvement opportunities.
   • Strengthen controls where necessary.

CORE PRINCIPLE:
“Measure accurately. Detect early. Correct the cause. Prevent recurrence.”

quality_concepts.title: Learn SQC
quality_concepts.description:
LEARN SQC — STATISTICAL QUALITY CONTROL

1. UNDERSTAND VARIATION
   • Learn why processes naturally vary.
   • Distinguish normal variation from unusual variation.
   • Understand how variation affects quality and consistency.

2. COLLECT QUALITY DATA
   • Collect accurate and relevant process data.
   • Use consistent measurement methods.
   • Ensure data is reliable before making decisions.

3. ANALYZE THE DATA
   • Use statistical methods to understand process behavior.
   • Identify patterns, trends and unusual observations.
   • Convert data into meaningful quality information.

4. USE CONTROL CHARTS
   • Monitor process performance over time.
   • Identify signals that may indicate special causes.
   • Take action when the process shows significant changes.

5. CONTROL PROCESS PERFORMANCE
   • Maintain processes within defined requirements and control limits.
   • Investigate abnormal variation promptly.
   • Use appropriate corrective and preventive actions.

6. IMPROVE WITH EVIDENCE
   • Use statistical evidence to guide improvement decisions.
   • Reduce unnecessary variation and defects.
   • Verify whether improvements produce sustained results.

CORE PRINCIPLE:
“Use reliable data and statistical thinking to understand variation, control processes and improve quality.”
